scope: Theorem 5.1 (Algebraic edge potential with markings) of the manuscript “A marked tensor obstruction to four-dimensional disk embedding” (preprints/A-marked-tensor-obstruction-to-four-dimensional-disk-embedding-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 305 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6453a6d9ab0cf566), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Put N = dim(H1(C) ⊗ sl2), R = C[[h1, . . . , hN ]], and J = Jac(f). There are an invertible formal coordinate change x = φ(h) and an algebraic power series F(x) ∈ (x)3 such that f(h) = F(φ(h)). Fix a torus basepoint and any finite collection of based loops in Y . For every matrix entry of their holonomies on the central critical scheme Spf(R/J), there is an algebraic power series in the x-coordinates whose pullback is that entry. In particular this holds for the based β-holonomy. The coordinate change can be chosen to identify these markings on the entire, possibly nonreduced, critical scheme.
